chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people: does one cow suffice for them? He said, 'As for the Hady (sacrifice for Hajj), no; and as for the Udhiyah (Eid sacrifice), yes.'

And the other view is that this applies only in the state of necessity, and it has already passed in the elaborations of these narrations what indicates that, and adds to its clarification what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلضَّرُورَةِ: Necessity (a legal state allowing exceptions to general rules)
key_terms.اَلْأَضَاحِيِّ: The Udhiyah, the sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.اَلْهَدْيِ: The Hady, the sacrificial animal offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Does one cow suffice for multiple people in Islamic sacrificial rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between Hady and Udhiyah, establishing that while a single cow suffices for a group in Eid al-Adha sacrifices, it does not for Hajj offerings. The text further introduces a secondary scholarly opinion limiting this group permissibility to cases of necessity, reflecting the nuanced development of Shia fiqh regarding communal sacrificial obligations.
